chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated that his father Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from his father al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Qasbani, from someone who mentioned him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The boy is instructed in fasting between fifteen and sixteen years of age.
ai.seo_question: At what age should a child be trained to fast according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the specific window of fifteen to sixteen years as the period for *ta'dib* (disciplined training) rather than immediate obligation. This distinction reflects the Shia juristic principle that while the age of *bulugh* (maturity) is typically marked by physical signs, the preparatory phase for fasting is intentionally set slightly earlier to ensure children are adequately conditioned before the full burden of the commandment applies.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 15-3 Ja’far ibn Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih al-Kufy - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father Ali ibn al-Hassan quoted his father Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih al-Kufy, on the authority of Al-Ab’bas ibn Amer al-Qasbani, on the authority of someone who quoted Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
A child should be instructed to fast when he is fifteen or sixteen years old.”
